paragraphs: Shmuel the Small (Avot chapter 4). Pious and humble. When they entered to intercalate the years and there were more than seven, he said he had come without permission to learn the halakhah, so as not to embarrass his colleague, and rose to leave. Rabban Gamliel the Elder told him—so Semahot chapter 8; Responsa Ralbah, folio 289, column 4, writes that he was in Rabban Gamliel the Elder's time, as in Semahot, contrary to Ra'avad, who placed him in the second Rabban Gamliel's time, called Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh—‘Sit, my son; all the years are worthy to be intercalated through you’: Sanhedrin 11a; Semahot chapter 8. He knew astronomy like Shmuel the priest, Yarhina'ah. He instituted the blessing against the sectarians before Rabban Gamliel the Elder (see above, Shimon Ha-Pakuli). He died without a son; they placed his key and notebook in his coffin. Rabban Gamliel the Elder and R' Elazar ben Azarya eulogized him: Semahot chapter 8. This needs examination: Rabban Gamliel the Elder died eighteen years before the destruction, while R' Elazar ben Azarya was no more than fourteen when the Temple was destroyed. How could R' Elazar ben Azarya have eulogized him with Rabban Gamliel the Elder? Perhaps it is a scribal error and the initials should be expanded as R' Elazar ben Arakh. At his death, near the destruction, he prophesied in Aramaic concerning Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and R' Yishmael ben Elisha the High Priest: ‘to execution’—they were killed at the destruction—as in Sanhedrin's first chapter there; end of Sotah, Jerusalem Talmud 9:13; Midrash Hazit, on ‘If she is a wall.’ Once they reclined in the upper room of Beit Gurya at Jericho. A heavenly voice issued: ‘There is one here worthy that the Divine Presence rest upon him like Moshe our teacher, but the generation is not worthy.’ They set their eyes on Hillel the Elder. When he died, they said of him, ‘Alas, pious one! Alas, humble one! Ezra's pupil.’ Again they reclined in an upper room at Yavneh; a heavenly voice issued, etc.; they set their eyes on Shmuel the Small. When he died they said, ‘Alas, pious one,’ etc., ‘one of Hillel's pupils’: there. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Sotah: a heavenly voice issued in Beit Gadya's upper room, ‘Two are worthy of divine inspiration; Hillel is one of them.’ They set their eyes on Shmuel the Small. In an upper room at Yavneh—that is, in Rabban Gamliel the Elder's days, see there—a heavenly voice issued: ‘Two are worthy of divine inspiration; Shmuel the Small is one.’ They set their eyes on R' Eliezer ben Hyrkanos, and rejoiced that their judgment agreed with Heaven's. End quotation. Why was he called Small? Because he made himself small; some say because he was only slightly below Shmuel of Ramah: there. He was a spark of Moshe: Megalleh Amukkot, 189. Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai was his colleague. Yosi ben Yohanan in his name.
